structure.value: The package is divided by concern so that parallel stories land in different files. card.py owns the Card dataclass and card parsing (parse_card, _load_cards, _as_cards, _parse_date). metrics.py owns the pure metric calculations (cycle time, lead time, throughput, WIP-limit violations, blocked-card aging, escalation rate, first-attempt rate, failure breakdown, top failure causes) and their helpers (_mean_days, _state_windows, _peak_occupancy, _load_wip_limits, ALL_METRICS). thresholds.py owns the default thresholds (DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS), calculate_flags, _load_thresholds, and _flag. report.py owns the single-sprint formatters (table, markdown, Prometheus, JSON), the markdown section and display helpers (_summary_section, _summary_counts, _sprint_section, _prior_sprint_section, _signed, _format_failure_breakdown, _METRIC_COLUMNS, _CANONICAL_ORDER, API_VERSION). sprint_range.py owns sprint-label and range parsing (_parse_sprint_label, _parse_sprint_range, _load_sprints) and the per-sprint range formatters (table, JSON, markdown). schema.py owns the JSON Schema documents for the API response (SINGLE_SPRINT_SCHEMA, SPRINT_RANGE_SCHEMA, METRIC_KEYS), used by the --schema flag. serve.py owns the scrape HTTP server (serve_metrics and its handler). cli.py owns main, argument parsing, and file I/O (_read). _docs_gen.py owns the generation of the marked (generated) sections for each docs/ file: it reads the code (calculate_* docstrings, _METRIC_COLUMNS, ALL_METRICS, schema documents, parse_card, cli argument help) and produces the text written between BEGIN/END markers in each docs/ file. changes.why: §19.8 requires the image to run as a user other than root. Research in crew#335 established that hadolint passes a Dockerfile with no USER at all, so the protection is a runtime uid check in CI, but the fix is in the Dockerfile.
changes.work: Add `RUN useradd --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin appuser` followed by `USER appuser` after the pip install step in the Dockerfile, so the image is installed as root but runs as appuser.

changes.what: Pin the Dockerfile base image by SHA-256 digest
changes.was: The Dockerfile uses `FROM python:3.12-slim` (a floating tag with no digest)
changes.why: §19.8 requires the image to be built from a base pinned by digest, so that a build is reproducible and not subject to silent tag drift on the registry.
changes.work: Replace the floating tag in the Dockerfile's FROM instruction with the current digest of python:3.12-slim, e.g. `FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:<64-hex>`, obtained from `docker manifest inspect` or the Docker Hub API.

changes.what: Add a Dependabot configuration covering the Dockerfile base image
changes.was: No .github/dependabot.yml or equivalent dependency-updater configuration exists in the repository
changes.why: §19.8 requires the pinned base digest to be kept current by a dependency updater, so the team does not manually re-pin the digest on every Python point release.
changes.work: Add .github/dependabot.yml with version 2 and an updates entry for package-ecosystem docker at directory / on a weekly schedule.

changes.what: Extend the docker-smoke CI job in tests.yml to prove all four §19.8 properties on every pull request
changes.was: The docker-smoke job only builds the image and runs `docker run --rm sprint-metrics-smoke sprint-metrics --help` then greps for 'usage:'. It does not check non-root, digest pinning, service-mode reachability from outside the container, or the presence of a dependency updater.

changes.why: §19.8: the service mode must be 'reached the way a user reaches it.' A user who runs the container needs the docker run -d -p ... --scrape invocation documented. The CI docker-contract job mirrors this invocation.
changes.work: Add a Container subsection to docs/scrape.md (outside the generated markers) showing docker run -d -p 9100:9100 -v $(pwd)/cards.json:/app/cards.json ghcr.io/mqucifer/sprint-metrics:X.Y.Z --scrape --port 9100 cards.json.

proposal.summary: The design records what already exists (Python 3.12, no runtime dependencies, standard-library-only, ruff+pytest local checks, module structure, release workflow) and adds the §19.8 container contract: the Dockerfile gains an ENTRYPOINT so the program name is not repeated, a non-root USER, and a digest-pinned base kept current by Dependabot. A new docker-contract job in tests.yml replaces the existing docker-smoke job and proves all four §19.8 assertions on every pull request. The README and docs/scrape.md document the container invocations that the CI proof validates against.
